name: v1.108.1
body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). This release is signed with the key introduced in [commit `e82a3c6`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the published signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.108.1
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.108.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.108.1
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---
## What's Changed
* ci: run the OSV scan and unit tests on stable, rc and lts branches (#50086) [backport lts/1.108.x] by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/50088
* test: fix stale unit tests on 1.108 LTS by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/50091
* fix(backport): backport 21 main fixes plus 2 prerequisites to lts/1.108.x for v1.108.1 by @kerry-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/50136
* fix(passthrough): skip team deployments when picking proxy-wide pass-through credentials on lts/1.108.x by @kerry-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/50217


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/compare/v1.108.0...v1.108.1

name: v1.107.0-rc.3
body:
## Verify this release

This release candidate is built from [`f9778e9`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/f9778e945daf481495272d68283d51bd72002f7c), the reviewed merge of #50129 into `rc/1.107.0`. It is published as `1.107.0rc3` on PyPI and `v1.107.0-rc.3` on Docker

After the Oct 21 incident (#47826) we replaced the cosign key that signs our Docker images. These images are signed with the new key from [commit `e82a3c6`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065)

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.107.0-rc.3
```

## Why a new 1.107 release candidate

Some users are still running the 1.107 release candidates and needed two GitHub Copilot fixes for per-user credentials. This release brings those fixes to that line. If you are not on a 1.107 release candidate, [1.108.0](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/releases/tag/v1.108.0) is the current stable

## What's new in 1.107.0-rc.3

2 PRs. 1 added, 1 fixed. No action needed to upgrade

### Changes

- **Other providers:** Added GitHub Copilot per-user credentials on GHE.com tenants with the new optional `github_copilot_host` field (#47610)
- **Other providers:** Fixed GitHub Copilot per-user connect failing with `no Copilot access found` when `GITHUB_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID` is set (#50116)

---

Backport #50129 · [Full changelog](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/compare/v1.107.0-rc.2...v1.107.0-rc.3)

name: v1.106.7
body:
## Verify this release

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.7
```

Same command for `litellm-database`, `litellm-non_root` and the `docker.io/litellm/*` images

## What's new in 1.106.7

We are readjusting how beta features work alongside LiteLLM, our core product. Starting with 1.106.7, the Lens beta is no longer packaged with the proxy or its Helm charts. If you use Lens today, v1.106.6 keeps working as it does now

2 PRs. 1 added, 1 changed. 1 needs action

### Action required

- **Lens:** If your Helm values set `lensWorker.enabled`, remove it before upgrading so the chart renders (#49173)

### Changes

- **Embeddings, images and audio:** Added `/v1/videos` support for custom providers registered in `custom_provider_map` (#49802)
- **Lens:** Moved the Lens beta out of the proxy package and Helm charts (#49173)

---

[Full changelog](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/compare/v1.106.6...v1.106.7)

name: v1.109.0-rc.1
body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). This release is signed with the key introduced in [commit `e82a3c6`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the published signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.109.0-rc.1
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.109.0-rc.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.109.0-rc.1
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). This release is signed with the key introduced in [commit `e82a3c6`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the published signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.109.0-dev.2
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.109.0-dev.2/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.109.0-dev.2
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

name: v1.109.0-dev.1
body:
## Verify this release ```bash cosign verify \ --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065/cosign.pub \ ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.109.0-dev.1 ``` Same command for `litellm-database`, `litellm-non_root` and the `docker.io/litellm/*` images ## What's new in 1.109.0-dev.1 704 PRs. 113 added, 312 fixed, 46 changed, 11 improved, 8 removed. 15 need action ### Action required - **Deployment:** Update image verification to use the new `cosign.pub` key (#48103) - **Chat completions:** Guard `chunk.choices[0]` reads with `if chunk.choices:` when `include_usage` is set (#47109) - **Vertex AI and Gemini:** Set `drop_params: true` or stop sending `temperature`, `top_p` and `top_k` to Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite and newer (#47645) - **Cost tracking and pricing:** Read `max_input_tokens` and `max_output_tokens` instead of `max_tokens` from the cost map (#48471) - **Anthropic:** Set `max_tokens` on requests to unmapped Anthropic models, or set `DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_CHAT_MAX_TOKENS` to 4096 (#48502) - **AWS Bedrock:** Set `streaming_buffer_until_moderated: true` on the guardrail if `converse-stream` replies still need masking (#46307) - **Logging and observability:** Set the GCS bucket and service account in proxy config instead of per request (#48599) - **Token counting:** Set a provider key on deployments used with count endpoints, since a local estimate is no longer returned (#46815) - **Keys, teams and auth:** Make `budget_duration` and `budget_id` changes on keys as an admin, since owners and team members now get 403 (#47681) - **Keys, teams and auth:** If `personal_key_model_access_from_teams` is on, grant needed MCP servers and agents to owners' teams first (#46293) - **Routing and fallbacks:** Add the `tag_routing_prefix` to caller routing tags, or move them to the key or team (#47428) - **Chat completions:** Handle 408 `litellm.Timeout` and `request_timeout` where you matched 500 `APIConnectionError` or `server_error` (#47198) - **Deployment:** Set `image_tag` or all four `*_image` URIs when sourcing the Terraform module from a git ref (#46960) - **Vertex AI and Gemini:** Raise a low `tpm` on Gemini TTS deployments, since limits now count TTS tokens (#44551) - **AWS Bedrock:** Increase budgets for keys or teams that run a traced `guardrailConfig` on every Bedrock call (#48278) ### Highlights - **Admin UI:** Added a Chat UI with a model hub, image generation and usage metrics (#48108) - **Routing and fallbacks:** Added mid-stream fallback continuation so a streaming chat cut off mid-answer continues on the configured fallback (#41127) - **SDK:** Fixed tool calls on `completion()` and `responses()` failing with `No module named 'mcp'` on base SDK installs, broken since v1.106.0 (#45961) - **Other providers:** Added OpenInfer as an OpenAI-compatible provider with `openinfer/` calls and spend tracking (#41034) - **Other providers:** Added xAI X Search to the Search API and WebSearch interception, with citation URLs and cost tracking (#48677) - **Deployment:** Added `LITELLM_OFFLINE_MODE` to turn off every fetch LiteLLM makes on its own with one switch (#48096) - **Cost tracking and pricing:** Added `model_info.pricing_provider` to price a deployment from another provider's catalog rates instead of $0 (#47620) - **Vertex AI and Gemini:** Added Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS support, including multi-speaker voices and `mp3`, `opus`, `alaw` and `mulaw` output (#31915) - **Agents:** Added `agent_access_default_deny` to stop keys with no agent grants from reaching every agent (#43979) ### More changes by area
OpenAI (10) - Added per-deployment workload identity on non-chat routes, realtime and the moderation guardrail (#39966) - Added OpenAI `gpt-6.1-terra` with pricing (#48429) - Fixed `prompt_cache_retention` such as `24h` being silently dropped instead of sent upstream (#47480) - Fixed 12-hour prompt cache writes on `openai/gpt-5.6` and newer billing at the 30-minute rate (#48088) - Plus 6 smaller fixes and updates (#43935, #44021, #46967, #47954, #48066, #48246)
Azure (18) - Fixed `/v1/responses` 404 on dated `api_version` deployments and `azure_ai` Grok reasoning token billing (#46377) - Fixed Azure realtime over WebRTC failing with a 404 on `client_secrets` and an invalid token on the SDP exchange (#47316) - Improved Entra auth by reusing credentials across requests and refreshing tokens off the event loop (#47348) - Plus 15 smaller fixes and updates (#43955, #46421, #46539, #46969, #47292, #47567, #47779, #48032, #48033, #48118, #48224, #48252, #48434, #48475, #48529)
Anthropic (10) - Fixed a fake `[System: ...]` message being added to tool-call-only assistant turns sent to Anthropic (#34822) - Fixed Claude `json_schema` answers losing keys listed only in `required` and escaping non-ASCII characters, broken since v1.107.0-rc.1 (#47478) - Fixed replayed `redacted_thinking` blocks being dropped, and Bedrock Converse 400s when sent twice (#47489) - Fixed streamed responses leaving native web search fees out of the reconstructed usage cost (#48528) - Plus 6 smaller fixes and updates (#41397, #46102, #46741, #47394, #47987, #48633)
AWS Bedrock (33) - Fixed Bedrock geo models priced at $0 and `dictionary changed size during iteration` errors during price reloads (#41523) - Fixed 400 `invalid beta flag` on Claude Code auto mode requests that carry no `safeguards` (#44471) - Fixed Nova Sonic `/v1/realtime` tool calls arriving with empty `arguments` and sessions breaking on flat tools (#46214) - Fixed `post_call` guardrails not scanning Claude output on `invoke-with-response-stream` passthrough (#46524) - Fixed Claude `json_schema` streams dropping reasoning and thinking blocks and ending on `tool_calls` with no tool calls (#46863) - Fixed JSON schema requests failing on Fable 5 and Sonnet 4.6 and losing adaptive thinking on Haiku 5.5 (#46870) - Fixed Bedrock Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 dropping reasoning on `json_schema` requests by trying native output first (#47100) - Fixed AWS region lookups through Vault blocking the event loop and stalling other requests on the worker (#47331) - Fixed Converse profile calls recording zero or wrong spend and partial custom prices dropping token charges (#47419) - Changed passthrough errors to the AWS shape so AWS SDKs read the error code and message and retry throttling (#46522) - Changed `/bedrock` pass-through routes to apply a model's `guardrailConfig`, returning 400 if Bedrock cannot use it (#47429) - Plus 22 smaller fixes and updates (#43875, #45453, #45992, #46670, #46936, #46987, #47000, #47040, #47144, #47196, #47202, #47211, #47226, #47260, #47283, #47441, #47462, #48150, #48247, #48441, #48479, #48682)
Vertex AI and Gemini (30) - Added an opt-in free-tier allowance so Google Search grounding spend matches the GCP invoice (#47494) - Fixed streamed Vertex AI pass-through calls missing the regional 10% uplift and custom deployment prices (#44795) - Fixed cache-marked requests listing all `cachedContents` on every call and creating duplicate caches (#46857) - Fixed audio prompt tokens billing $0 and video or image tokens ignoring the above-200k tier price (#47373) - Fixed `text-embedding-005` and `text-multilingual-embedding-002` billing per token instead of per character (#47460) - Fixed Gemini 2.5 rejecting tool results with images and the history replay that follows, broken since v1.89.0 (#48428) - Fixed slow Google credential requests blocking the proxy worker on Claude `/v1/messages` (#48523) - Plus 23 smaller fixes and updates (#36460, #40868, #41683, #44908, #46793, #46826, #47134, #47185, #47294, #47404, #47447, #47466, #47542, #47646, #47666, #47847, #48085, #48086, #48248, #48430, #48442, #48587, #48690)
Other providers (69) - Added ChatGPT subscription forwarding so Codex or Pi users keep their login behind a separate LiteLLM key (#41522) - Added Volcengine Doubao-Seedance video generation on `/v1/videos`, with prices for the four models (#46156) - Added Nace as a provider with Drex decision models, available in Add Model (#46523) - Added DeepSeek as a `/v1/search` provider with `search_provider: deepseek` (#47401) - Added `/v1/extraction` endpoint with Cloudflare Clairic support (#47473) - Added OpenCode Go routing, pricing and model discovery (#48140) - Added the Refuseless provider with model pricing and capability metadata (#48497) - Added Abliteration model pricing and capabilities, and fixed `reasoning_effort` being dropped (#48498) - Fixed SageMaker streams that lost part of the answer or usage, and failed streams now return an error (#47495) - Fixed Groq HTTP 400 on the next turn after reusing a streamed reasoning reply as history (#48268) - Plus 59 smaller fixes and updates (#33121, #38736, #39227, #40152, #40605, #41021, #45092, #45567, #46091, #46171, #46792, #46794, #46795, #46945, #46959, #46964, #46991, #47085, #47132, #47252, #47253, #47254, #47291, #47318, #47326, #47346, #47370, #47371, #47395, #47423, #47424, #47487, #47492, #47518, #47570, #47591, #47610, #47667, #47690, #47784, #47785, #47963, #48121, #48158, #48244, #48251, #48254, #48265, #48270, #48448, #48450, #48453, #48455, #48522, #48527, #48621, #48651, #48668, #48676)
Chat completions (6) - Fixed chat streams failing with a proxy error when progress chunks have no choice index (#46947) - Plus 5 smaller fixes and updates (#39762, #44349, #46928, #47790, #48052)
Responses API (17) - Fixed non-stream MCP auto-execute on `/v1/responses` logging and billing only one of its two model calls (#43667) - Fixed later turns on an open Responses WebSocket skipping deployment checks and not counting toward budgets (#45727) - Fixed `/v1/responses` on Claude dropping returned and replayed `compaction` items (#46754) - Fixed native WebSocket connections writing one summed spend-log row at close instead of one per `response.create` turn (#46768) - Fixed Responses WebSocket running `pre_call` guardrails on turn one only and rebilling that cost every turn (#47013) - Fixed OpenAI pass-through `GET /responses/{id}` being billed again on every call (#47171) - Fixed background spend not counting toward the key's project or per-model budgets (#47504) - Fixed 500 when replaying `web_search_call` input items that have no `action` (#48417) - Fixed audio, PDF and image tool results and history media being dropped in Responses and Gemini conversions (#48484) - Plus 8 smaller fixes and updates (#31074, #46662, #46724, #47445, #47506, #47688, #48119, #48686)
Messages API (10) - Fixed retried `/v1/messages` attempts mixing up usage and spend logs, and exhausted retries billing only the last (#45194) - Fixed 400 `Tool reference not found` for tool names over 64 chars when a guardrail rewrites `/v1/messages` (#47434) - Fixed `stop_sequences` being ignored for OpenAI models on `/v1/messages` (#48534) - Fixed `/v1/messages` streams reporting zero `input_tokens` in `message_start` when bridged to Chat Completions (#48618) - Plus 6 smaller fixes and updates (#45136, #46096, #46749, #47123, #47347, #48220)
Realtime (1) - Fixed sessions going silent when a transcript guardrail sent `turn_detection` with no `type` to OpenAI (#44939)
Embeddings, images and audio (1) - Added a per-request input batch limit on `/v1/embeddings` to cap how many inputs one call can send (#44574)
Batches and files (8) - Added routing of `POST /v1/batches` to batch deployments and `supported_endpoints` on `/model_group/info` (#47376) - Fixed 400 on `GET /files/{id}/content` with raw `gs://` file ids from the unmanaged Vertex batch flow, broken since v1.90.0 (#40621) - Fixed fine-tuning jobs failing with 400 for files uploaded with `target_model_names` (#46552) - Fixed 403 when team keys retrieve, cancel or download their own batches (#47067) - Fixed batch cost logging crashing before the batch is marked processed when every request fails (#47155) - Fixed batch spend going unrecorded when a provider returns malformed response envelopes or metadata writes fail (#47184) - Fixed batch cost tracking being starved by older retryable batches and losing spend on completed ones (#47190) - Fixed completed batches staying permanently unbilled after a temporary accounting failure (#47625)
Vector stores (3) - Fixed `/rag/ingest` and `/rag/query` ignoring team provider credentials and denying viewers and team JWTs (#45497) - Fixed team key vector store search failing when the team's first model is from a different provider (#46894) - Fixed proxy-created OpenAI vector stores filling all 16 metadata slots and then failing updates with HTTP 400 (#47021)
Token counting (11) - Added `token_count_framing` and `token_count_model` settings and a count source in token count responses (#46777) - Fixed `/v1/messages/count_tokens` on Gemini dropping PDFs, images and tool blocks, and 500s on AI Studio (#46759, #46767, #46772) - Fixed DeepSeek V4 token counts missing Azure's billed tokens by using DeepSeek's own tokenizer (#47173, #47353) - Changed Responses input token counts to match inference, fixing Claude counts with tools and `text.format` (#47363) - Plus 7 smaller fixes and updates (#46583, #46839, #46843, #47163, #47586, #48526, #48624)
MCP (27) - Added support for redeeming an ID-JAG as an RFC 7523 `jwt-bearer` grant on the gateway token endpoint (#46748) - Fixed `tools/list` returning an empty list when servers answer 429, now retried with an error if all fail (#46649) - Fixed the caller's LiteLLM key being forwarded to upstream MCP servers when `Authorization` is in `extra_headers` (#46932) - Fixed VS Code sign-in to DCR bridge MCP servers when the upstream rejects loopback redirect URIs, broken since v1.103.0 (#46940) - Fixed large MCP SSE tool results failing, and invalid size limits breaking MCP discovery and tool calls, broken since v1.103.0 (#47034) - Fixed MCP OAuth sign-in callback returning 403 behind AWS WAF by sealing the `litellm_cp_return_to` cookie (#47595) - Fixed per-user auth MCP servers missing from `/mcp-rest/tools/list` and `/mcp` `tools/list`, broken since v1.104.2 (#47677) - Fixed a readonly MCP toolset URL returning every tool instead of only the toolset's tools, broken since v1.106.0 (#48095) - Fixed revoked or expired browser sessions still being accepted during gateway authorization (#48494) - Plus 18 smaller fixes and updates (#41197, #44125, #44957, #46264, #46513, #46745, #46747, #46968, #46994, #47004, #47094, #47569, #47897, #48424, #48474, #48622, #48625, #48669)
Agents (2) - Added the pi harness to `litellm.agent()` and fixed harness turn `cost` ignoring prompt cache prices (#45467) - Fixed OpenCode via `litellm.agent()` using the script's folder instead of the sandbox, and hanging on resume (#47530)
Guardrails (10) - Added a native Reco guardrail that blocks requests on Reco errors unless `fail_on_error: false` (#48243) - Fixed guardrail masks on messages and tools not reaching Bedrock Converse requests (#45874) - Fixed corrupted numbered PII tokens in Presidio when one value matches several entities with `output_parse_pii` (#47024) - Fixed `hide-secrets` missing secrets in tool results, tool inputs, `tool_calls` arguments, and system prompts (#47122) - Fixed pass-through guardrails scanning `litellm_metadata` fields added by LiteLLM, which caused false matches (#48276) - Changed guardrail blocks mid-stream to end chat completions streams with an error event, not a cut connection (#46953) - Plus 4 smaller fixes and updates (#46338, #46606, #46673, #46965)
Caching (1) - Fixed streamed cache hits dropping prompt cache token counts from `usage`, including on `/v1/messages` (#47073)
Routing and fallbacks (29) - Added Kubernetes pod discovery to spread load across pods behind a headless service `api_base` (#44342, #44393, #44666) - Fixed region, RPM and param pre-call checks being skipped when the router cannot token-count a request (#44544) - Fixed `stream_timeout` cutting off slow answers when Bedrock serves a `stream=True` call without streaming (#47162) - Fixed key and team `router_settings` reaching the provider and dropping retries, fallbacks and timeout (#47257) - Fixed 500s from `router_settings.default_priority` or an integer `priority`, and now reject a malformed `priority` (#47498) - Fixed `IndexError` and wrong deployment lookups when deployments are deleted or added concurrently (#47680) - Fixed the router sending image requests to `supports_vision: false` deployments in mixed model groups (#48149, #48152) - Fixed 500s on every request to a model group after one negative or NaN latency sample under latency routing, broken since v1.102.0 (#48216) - Fixed image requests reaching declared text-only deployments unless `enable_pre_call_checks` was on (#48241) - Fixed one caller's exhausted forwarded Claude subscription putting the shared model into cooldown for others (#48485) - Fixed proxy-wide wildcard deployments shadowing a team's own wildcard deployment for that team's keys (#48490) - Changed per-deployment `reasoning_effort_levels` to apply on every provider and route, including `azure_ai` (#46601) - Changed router `allowed_fails` to keep a lone deployment with no fallback in rotation instead of returning 429 (#48644) - Plus 16 smaller fixes and updates (#45795, #46197, #46263, #46390, #46411, #47120, #47406, #47565, #47617, #47727, #48175, #48206, #48470, #48627, #48632, #48645)
Cost tracking and pricing (33) - Added one spend row per timed-out retry attempt with `num_retries`, so spend matches the provider invoice (#47416) - Fixed cached and reasoning token counts dropped from streamed usage, pricing streams at the full input rate (#36678) - Fixed Responses API image generation and usage-reported web search missing from `cost_breakdown.tool_usage_cost` (#41877) - Fixed streams with no backend usage being recorded at 0 tokens and $0 instead of the token estimate, broken since v1.104.0-dev.1 (#44230) - Fixed background interactions going unbilled after a crash, a late restart or on models with their own `api_key` (#45743) - Fixed calls billing $0 when the response model name only matches a price-free capability rule (#47037) - Fixed Tavily `advanced` and Linkup `deep` searches being billed at the basic and standard prices (#47411) - Fixed chat completions MCP auto-execute spend rows pricing only the first of its two paid model calls (#47422) - Fixed requests that time out at the provider logging $0 spend instead of their estimated input cost (#47435, #47436, #47437) - Fixed deployments with `model_info.base_model` such as `azure/eu/o3` billing $0 on every request (#47497) - Fixed non-streamed requests adding double their recorded cost to key spend (#47510) - Fixed spend log batches being dropped when Postgres restarts mid-flush, so requests lost their spend row (#47571) - Fixed missing spend rows when clients disconnect from streamed `/v1/responses` and OpenAI or Azure `/v1/messages` (#47611) - Fixed spend priced from a caller-sent `base_model` and rows lost to lone surrogates in multipart `metadata` (#47639) - Fixed key, team, user and daily spend rows being dropped when the proxy stops right after a request (#48131) - Fixed Price Data Reload wiping custom pricing of DB models, which logged $0 spend on `/v1/messages` (#48486) - Plus 17 smaller fixes and updates (#46972, #46975, #47114, #47307, #47561, #47568, #47623, #47647, #47648, #47652, #47655, #47658, #48259, #48261, #48275, #48433, #48620)
Logging and observability (33) - Added `maximum_spend_logs_size` to delete the oldest spend logs first once they exceed a size limit (#47450, #47451, #47500) - Fixed Responses `instructions` still reaching request and response logs when message logging is turned off (#43315) - Fixed intermittent 500 `dictionary changed size during iteration` when caching or a sync callback is on (#46044) - Fixed provider-side 401s missing from `litellm_deployment_failure_responses` and `litellm_deployment_state`, broken since v1.80.13 (#46668) - Fixed the proxy printing plaintext at startup with `json_logs` on, so the banner and model list are now JSON (#47035) - Changed `langfuse_otel` to set trace-level name, input, output and tags on traces LiteLLM starts (#42705) - Changed rate-limited model groups to return `rate_limit_error` and Sentry to start at boot without stack locals (#46344) - Plus 26 smaller fixes and updates (#41150, #42740, #43594, #43604, #44185, #44187, #44199, #45555, #45597, #46956, #47019, #47045, #47124, #47129, #47156, #47175, #47182, #47183, #47192, #47384, #47449, #47456, #47468, #47848, #48239, #48613)
Keys, teams and auth (19) - Fixed `/team/block` and `/team/unblock` not applying to cached teams until the cache expired (#35643) - Fixed end-user budget resets never committing once `LiteLLM_EndUserTable` has millions of rows (#46502) - Fixed SAML SSO login 401 when the IdP callback lands on a different replica or worker (#46807) - Fixed lowered user, end-user or tag limits sometimes being ignored, and `max_budget` undercounting across workers (#46997) - Fixed SCIM group delete leaving memberships and members' team keys active, and removing members one at a time (#47544) - Fixed concurrency slots staying occupied after finished streams, so keys got rejected with SSE keepalive on (#48452) - Fixed team members' spend never resetting after a temporary budget increase on a member using the team default (#48495) - Changed free installs to refuse new SSO accounts past five users without locking out existing SSO users (#48097) - Plus 11 smaller fixes and updates (#41236, #44763, #46190, #46738, #46855, #46979, #47341, #47358, #48260, #48444, #48623)
Admin UI (54) - Changed the Chat page to be on by default, and `enable_chat_ui: false` still hides it (#46918) - Changed the Playground chat to a single composer with a Settings popover and a reply inspector panel (#46934) - Plus 52 smaller fixes and updates (#26667, #41350, #43425, #45674, #45893, #46064, #46778, #46830, #46834, #46941, #46978, #47025, #47065, #47440, #47552, #47612, #47630, #47653, #47662, #47671, #47974, #47998, #48074, #48081, #48082, #48094, #48105, #48106, #48107, #48109, #48123, #48124, #48137, #48199, #48207, #48223, #48225, #48425, #48431, #48451, #48454, #48456, #48464, #48478, #48487, #48488, #48500, #48504, #48532, #48629, #48630, #48634)
Deployment (12) - Added a pre-upgrade check for old spend-log rows that would fail the `(api_key, startTime)` index build (#48493) - Fixed `terraform apply` failing with `Status: 201 Created` on `litellm_mcp_server` and creating duplicates (#46550) - Fixed Terraform `additional_drop_params` deleting the keys it names instead of sending them to the proxy (#46782) - Removed the eMudhra root CA from certificates trusted by Python, Rust and the Docker image (#47670, #47969, #48139) - Plus 8 smaller fixes and updates (#43313, #46709, #46781, #47056, #47165, #47378, #48065, #48674)
SDK (4) - Plus 4 smaller fixes and updates (#48266, #48359, #48615, #48650)
Performance (11) - Fixed memory growth on proxies without Redis, which queued a budget spend increment per request (#46831) - Improved streaming so long buffered streams no longer stall other requests on the same worker (#46925) - Improved proxy latency by freezing the startup heap so gen-2 GC passes no longer pause requests for 0.6 to 0.8 s (#47137) - Plus 8 smaller fixes and updates (#46712, #46803, #47030, #47352, #47393, #47400, #47614, #48089)
Other (21) - Fixed 400 `Invalid JSON` on request bodies sent with `Content-Encoding: zstd` or `gzip` (#47418) - Plus 20 smaller fixes and updates (#43624, #44614, #46942, #47385, #47501, #47508, #47535, #47564, #47700, #47979, #47985, #48221, #48250, #48438, #48505, #48524, #48619, #48628, #48640, #48662)

## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). This release is signed with the key introduced in [commit `e82a3c6`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the published signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.108.0-rc.1
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.108.0-rc.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.108.0-rc.1
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---
## What's Changed
* fix: bring rc/1.108.0 to parity with the v1.106.x patch fixes by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/48691


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/compare/v1.107.0-rc.1...v1.108.0-rc.1

>
> New `cosign.pub` SHA-256: `e3fe3e08c44b16407fe0b37c43b4f8b603b3a0f4ee74c29e647bc022d762c2c0`

### Changes

- **Chat completions:** Fixed tool calls landing on `choices[1]` with gpt-5.4+ models, broken since v1.97.0 (#46099)
- **Messages API:** Fixed `/v1/messages` streams holding `message_start` for minutes during adaptive thinking on Bedrock and Vertex, broken since v1.100.0 (#43600)
- **Token counting:** Fixed DeepSeek and Qwen3.5 token counts running up to 30% low or twice too high on the count endpoints (#47685)
- **Token counting:** Changed `/v1/messages/count_tokens` to return HTTP 400 instead of a known-wrong local estimate (#47705)
- **Caching:** Fixed automatic prompt caching adding extra cache marks on `/v1/messages` when `extra_body` overrides a client mark (#43341)
- **Cost tracking and pricing:** Fixed the Usage API timing out while looking up names for busy hashed keys (#43656)
- **Cost tracking and pricing:** Fixed streamed requests through a model alias billing $0 instead of the deployment's price, broken since v1.92.0 (#44341)
- **Cost tracking and pricing:** Fixed large non-streaming chat requests to `openai/responses/*` models logging and charging spend twice, broken since v1.102.0 (#44508)
- **Cost tracking and pricing:** Fixed failed, timed-out, cancelled and spilled-over requests being priced wrong or not at all (#47718)
- **Cost tracking and pricing:** Fixed batch cost tracking, claude-haiku-5-5 and Bedrock profile pricing, and `safeguards` requests on `/v1/messages` (#47726) <sup>Also in [1.105.3](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/releases/tag/v1.105.3)</sup>
- **Admin UI:** Fixed Usage reports showing no owner for CLI session keys when spend logs are off or purged (#43642, #47805)

body:
## Verify this release

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.1
```

Same command for `litellm-database`, `litellm-non_root` and the `docker.io/litellm/*` images

## What's new in 1.106.1

9 PRs. 6 fixed. 1 needs action

### Action required

- **Vector stores:** Run `db_scripts/strip_vector_store_internal_metadata.py` to fix stores created before this release (#47021)

### Changes

- **Anthropic:** Fixed signed thinking blocks and `thinking.block_binding` being dropped on multi-turn requests (#41362, #46342) <sup>Also in [1.105.2](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/releases/tag/v1.105.2)</sup>
- **Chat completions:** Fixed tool calls landing on `choices[1]` with gpt-5.4+ models, broken since v1.97.0 (#46099) <sup>Also in [1.105.2](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/releases/tag/v1.105.2)</sup>
- **Batches and files:** Fixed 403 when team keys retrieve, cancel or download their own batches (#47067) <sup>Also in [1.105.2](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/releases/tag/v1.105.2)</sup>
- **Vector stores:** Fixed HTTP 400 on metadata updates caused by keys the proxy added to the store (#47021)
- **Token counting:** Fixed undercounted PDFs, system prompts and tools, and rejected Google `countTokens` requests (#47389, #47446, #47454) <sup>Also in [1.104.4](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/releases/tag/v1.104.4), [1.105.2](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/releases/tag/v1.105.2)</sup>
- **MCP:** Fixed `Tool not found` when calling a bare tool name on `/{server}/mcp`, broken since v1.103.0 (#46225)

---

name: v1.103.5
body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.103.5
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.103.5/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.103.5
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---
## What's Changed
* fix(responses): backport #46099 and #46109 to stable/1.103.x for v1.103.5 by @mrinal-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/46949

body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.107.0-dev.2
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.107.0-dev.2/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.107.0-dev.2
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

name: v1.106.0-rc.4
body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.0-rc.4
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.106.0-rc.4/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.0-rc.4
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---

name: v1.106.0-rc.3
body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.0-rc.3
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.106.0-rc.3/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.0-rc.3
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---
## What's Changed
* fix(guardrails): backport #46086 to rc/1.106.0 by @mateo-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/46383
* fix(prometheus): backport #46267 to rc/1.106.0 by @yucheng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/46491

name: v1.104.3
body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.104.3
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.104.3/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.104.3
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---
## What's Changed
* feat(guardrails): backport the decision model guardrail to stable/1.104.x (#45663) by @yucheng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/45900

name: v1.105.0-rc.2
body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.105.0-rc.2
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.105.0-rc.2/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.105.0-rc.2
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---

* chore(deps): refresh locked dependencies on rc/1.105.0 by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/44803
* chore(docker): bump pgbouncer to 1.26.0 by @devin-ai-integration[bot] in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/45013

body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.104.0
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.104.0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.104.0
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

name: v1.103.3
body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.103.3
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.103.3/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.103.3
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---
## What's Changed
* fix(proxy): enforce the migration check by default and stop building SpendLogs indexes in migrations (stable/1.103.x) by @devin-ai-integration[bot] in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/44205
* chore(release): bump litellm-proxy-extras 0.4.100 -> 0.4.100.post1 for stable/1.103.x by @devin-ai-integration[bot] in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/44225

* chore(release): backport #42643 to stable/1.103.x by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/44309

name: v1.103.2
body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.103.2
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.103.2/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.103.2
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---
## What's Changed
* chore(release): sync stable/1.103.x to v1.103.1 by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/43824
* fix(proxy): backport #40541, #43642, and #43656 to stable/1.103.x for v1.103.2 by @devin-ai-integration[bot] in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/43897

* fix(proxy): backport #43962 to stable/1.103.x by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/43984

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

```bash
cosign verify \
```

```bash
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.104.0-rc.2
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.104.0-rc.2/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.104.0-rc.2
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:

  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.104.0-dev.2
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.104.0-dev.2/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.104.0-dev.2
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

name: v1.100.3
body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.100.3
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.100.3/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.100.3
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---
## What's Changed
* chore(release): backport #39631, #39729, #40639 to stable/1.100.x and cut 1.100.3 by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/43132


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/compare/v1.100.2...v1.100.3

name: v1.102.1
body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.102.1
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.102.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.102.1
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---

## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.102.0
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.102.0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.102.0
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.103.0-dev.2
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.103.0-dev.2/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.103.0-dev.2
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.103.0-dev.1
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.103.0-dev.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.103.0-dev.1
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

name: v1.102.0-rc.2
body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.102.0-rc.2
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.102.0-rc.2/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.102.0-rc.2
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---
## What's Changed
* fix(responses): backport request-param leak fixes to rc/1.102.0 (#41018, #41141, #41144) by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/41342

name: v1.101.0
body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.101.0
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.101.0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.101.0
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.102.0-dev.2
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.102.0-dev.2/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.102.0-dev.2
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

name: v1.100.1
body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.100.1
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.100.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.100.1
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---

* chore(release): backport #39568 and #39572 to stable/1.100.x and cut 1.100.1 by @devin-ai-integration[bot] in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/40176

name: v1.101.0-rc.2
body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.101.0-rc.2
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.101.0-rc.2/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.101.0-rc.2
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---

* feat: backport MongoDB sidecar to rc/1.101.0 by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/40316

body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.100.0
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.100.0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.100.0
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.101.0-dev.2
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.101.0-dev.2/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.101.0-dev.2
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---
## What's Changed
* test: exempt MockTransport request-shape embedding tests from VCR replay by @mateo-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/39185
* fix(ui): render the logs Tools panel with theme tokens by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/39129
* fix(proxy): default max_idle_connection_lifetime to 60s on DB URLs by @devin-ai-integration[bot] in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/39134
* fix(mcp): follow tools/list pagination from upstream servers by @yucheng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/39172

name: v1.99.1
body:
## Docker-only release

**This release ships container images only. There is no PyPI package for `1.99.1`.**

`pip install litellm==1.99.1` will not resolve — install the images below, or stay on `1.99.0` on PyPI. The git tag and this release exist so the images are traceable to an exact commit.

| Image | Tags |
|---|---|
| `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm` · `docker.io/litellm/litellm` | `1.99.1`, `v1.99.1` |
| `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database` · `docker.io/litellm/litellm-database` | `1.99.1`, `v1.99.1` |
| `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-non_root` · `docker.io/litellm/litellm-non_root` | `1.99.1`, `v1.99.1` |

This is the newest stable image, so the rolling `latest` and `main-stable` image tags now point at `1.99.1`.

It carries one fix on top of `1.99.0`: OpenTelemetry v2 spans now emit cache token counts (`gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens` and `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens`) alongside the cache cost that was already reported. If you compute spend from OTel token counts rather than from LiteLLM's own cost fields, prompt-caching workloads were previously under-counted.

---
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.99.1
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.99.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.99.1
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---
## What's Changed
* chore(release): backport #38716 to stable/1.99.x and cut 1.99.1 by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/39179


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/compare/v1.99.0...v1.99.1

name: v1.97.1
body:
## Docker-only release

**This release ships container images only. There is no PyPI package for `1.97.1`.**

`pip install litellm==1.97.1` will not resolve — install the images below, or stay on `1.97.0` on PyPI. The git tag and this release exist so the images are traceable to an exact commit.

| Image | Tags |
|---|---|
| `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm` · `docker.io/litellm/litellm` | `1.97.1`, `v1.97.1` |
| `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database` · `docker.io/litellm/litellm-database` | `1.97.1`, `v1.97.1` |
| `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-non_root` · `docker.io/litellm/litellm-non_root` | `1.97.1`, `v1.97.1` |

This is a maintenance patch on the 1.97 line. It refreshes base-image and dependency pins to clear known CVEs and makes no change to LiteLLM behavior. The rolling `latest` and `main-stable` image tags are deliberately **not** moved by this release and continue to point at the newest stable line.

---
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.97.1
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.97.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.97.1
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---
## What's Changed
* chore(deps): refresh stale dependency pins and cut 1.97.1 by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/39200
* fix(docker): pin apk python to 3.13 and bump wolfi-base on stable/1.97.x (cherry-pick #38917 + #38973) by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/39212

name: v1.99.0-rc.2
body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.99.0-rc.2
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.99.0-rc.2/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.99.0-rc.2
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---
## What's Changed
* fix(ui): backport the shadcn migration regression fixes onto 1.99.0 by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/38821
* fix(e2e): backport the vertex realtime and vision image fixture fixes to rc/1.99.0 by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/38848
* fix(ui): drop stray text next to Close in the model connection test dialog by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/38854
* [Backport rc/1.99.0] fix(anthropic): translate tool_result document blocks in the /v1/messages bridge by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/38855
* test(e2e): backport the select-anchoring and router-fallback spec de-flakes by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/38862


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/compare/v1.99.0-rc.1...v1.99.0-rc.2

body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.100.0-dev.1
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.100.0-dev.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.100.0-dev.1
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---

body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.99.0-rc.1
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.99.0-rc.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.99.0-rc.1
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

name: v1.98.0
body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.98.0
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.98.0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.98.0
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.99.0-dev.2
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.99.0-dev.2/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.99.0-dev.2
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.99.0-dev.1
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.99.0-dev.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.99.0-dev.1
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

body:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.98.0-rc.1
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.98.0-rc.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.98.0-rc.1
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```
